title: Quiz: Total Quality Management and Cost of Poor Quality

questions.text: A data team spends £12,000 per year re-running failed ETL jobs and correcting bad data before it reaches the warehouse. This is which COPQ category?
questions.explanation: Rework and reprocessing before the output reaches the customer is an Internal Failure Cost — the defect was caught internally but still required resources to fix.

questions.text: Deming's 14 Points include 'Cease dependence on inspection to achieve quality.' Which TQM principle does this support?
options: Process-Centred Approach — build quality into the process
questions.explanation: This point supports the TQM principle of managing and improving the process. If the process is well-designed, inspection becomes unnecessary — quality is built in, not tested in.

questions.text: Crosby's phrase 'Quality is Free' means quality improvement has no cost.
questions.explanation: 'Quality is Free' means the cost of achieving quality (prevention + appraisal) is less than the cost of not achieving it (failures + rework + customer losses). Quality improvement does have a cost, but it pays for itself.

questions.text: A company loses £200,000 per year in customer churn due to inaccurate product recommendations. This is classified as:
questions.explanation: Customer churn due to quality failures is an External Failure Cost — the defect has reached the customer and caused business harm. This is the most expensive COPQ category.

questions.text: TQM requires that quality responsibility be distributed across all employees, not concentrated in a dedicated QC department.
questions.explanation: A core TQM principle is Total Employee Involvement — everyone from top management to frontline workers is responsible for quality. This contrasts with traditional approaches where QC is a separate inspection department.
